First Steps

KITCHEN NOTES / FIX COMMON MISTAKES

Taste, then decide

When something tastes off, most people panic and start dumping in random ingredients. There's a simpler order: salt, then acid, then fat.

Salt → Acid → Fat
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    Taste it plain first

    Before adding anything, taste a spoonful on its own and notice what feels missing.

    Look for You can describe it in one word: flat, dull, heavy, or sharp.

  2. 02

    Try salt first

    A small pinch, stirred in, tasted again. Salt usually solves "flat" before anything else does.

    Look for Other flavors suddenly taste more like themselves, not just saltier.

  3. 03

    Reach for acid next

    If it still tastes heavy or dull after salt, try a small squeeze of lemon or splash of vinegar.

    Look for The dish tastes brighter and lighter, like something lifted off it.

  4. 04

    Finish with fat if it needs rounding out

    Still tastes sharp or thin? A little olive oil, butter, or cheese can round it out.

    Look for The flavors feel connected instead of separate.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

You can name what changed after each adjustment, not just that "it tastes better now."

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Adding several ingredients at once to fix a vague "something is missing" feeling.

Fixing three things at once makes it impossible to know which one actually worked — or to undo it if you go too far.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Change one thing in a small amount, taste, then decide on the next.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

This order works on almost anything you cook — it is a way of tasting, not a technique tied to one recipe.

Still tastes off after all three?

That's useful information too — it might need more of the main ingredient or more time to cook, not something new.
